# AkindaCo Education and Training

> AkindaCo is a multidisciplinary clinical psychotherapy, family therapy, art therapy and
> Positive Behaviour Support practice in Adelaide, South Australia. This site holds its
> continuing professional development (CPD) training for therapists, mental health
> clinicians, school staff and early childhood educators, plus clinical supervision,
> student placements and guest lectures. All courses are taught by clinicians who hold
> current caseloads. Based at 183 Tynte St, North Adelaide SA, with rooms at Salisbury and
> 21 Philip Highway, Elizabeth. Programs are delivered in-house at organisations and
> across all areas of South Australia, including regional and remote.

Contact: hello@akindaco.com | 08 7081 5886
Main website: https://www.akindaco.com/
Positive Behaviour Support site: https://pbs.akindaco.com/
Bookings run on Humanitix: https://events.humanitix.com/host/akindaco

## Courses for therapists and mental health clinicians

- [Family therapy training Adelaide — Family Therapy Foundations](https://training.akindaco.com/family-therapy-training-adelaide/): Two-day PACFA-endorsed intensive in systemic family therapy. Next intake Thursday 17 to Friday 18 September 2026, 9:30am–4:30pm ACST, at 183 Tynte St, North Adelaide. Early Bird $340, individual seat $425, team of 3+ $918. No prior family therapy training required. Covers reading a family system, drawing a genogram live in the room, circular questions, multi-person sessions, and the self of the therapist. Book at https://events.humanitix.com/family-therapy-foundations-two-day-intensive-e62nyjcr
- [Art therapy training Adelaide — Art Therapy Foundations](https://training.akindaco.com/art-therapy-training-adelaide/): Two-day introductory course on the theoretical, psychological and ethical foundations of art therapy plus practical skills. Locations across Adelaide. Dates for the next intake being confirmed. No artistic skill or prior training needed.
- [Genogram training Adelaide — The Therapeutic Use of Genograms](https://training.akindaco.com/genogram-training-adelaide/): One-day course on genograms in assessment and intervention, including engaging children, managing high affect, creative modalities, cultural safety, and work with LGBTQIA+ clients and children in residential care. Salisbury and North Adelaide. Dates being confirmed.

## Programs for early childhood educators

Both early childhood programs run **all year round** with no fixed intake, so services can
reach out at any time. Both are approved Preschool Boost listings, delivered in-person
across all areas of South Australia including regional and remote. A free 30-minute
virtual consultation is available before committing. Travel within 10km of 183 Tynte St,
North Adelaide and 21 Philip Highway, Elizabeth is included in program cost; further
travel is charged at $285 per hour. Both programs are customised to the service, and
AkindaCo also builds off-the-menu training in these areas on request.

- [Preschool Boost: Attachment, Trauma & Child Development](https://training.akindaco.com/preschool-boost-attachment-trauma-child-development/): Six-unit series delivered in-service as 3-hour sequential training modules, dates arranged to suit. $285 per hour, so $855 per module. Attachment theory, developmental neuroscience and trauma-informed practice, with one-on-one mentorship and co-facilitation. Government listing: https://www.earlychildhood.sa.gov.au/for-providers/preschool-boost-for-early-childhood-services/search/provider?p=attachment-trauma-and-child-development&id=1703722
- [Preschool Boost: Learn to Play Group](https://training.akindaco.com/preschool-boost-learn-to-play/): Therapist-led weekly group based on Dr Karen Stagnitti's Learn to Play approach, delivered in your preschool room over 17 weeks. Each week is 30 minutes educator training, a 60-minute group, then 30 minutes reflection. $570 per weekly session. Government listing: https://www.earlychildhood.sa.gov.au/for-providers/preschool-boost-for-early-childhood-services/search/provider?p=learn-to-play-group&id=1703723
- AkindaCo also holds a third Preschool Boost listing, Various Allied Health Supports: https://www.earlychildhood.sa.gov.au/for-providers/preschool-boost-for-early-childhood-services/search/provider?p=various-allied-health-supports&id=1703736

## Supervision, placements and guest lectures

- **Clinical supervision** is offered by Shane Fotheringham, Rana Kökçinar, Paula Gillespie-Fotheringham and Kate Maitland, covering systemic and family therapy, art psychotherapy, positive behaviour support, child and adolescent work, perinatal and infant mental health, and complex adult practice.
- **Student clinical placements** are taken from the University of Adelaide, IKON Institute and some interstate providers including the University of Melbourne. Students stay for the whole year and specialise either in working with children and young people or in working with adults. Placements for professionals interested in positive behaviour support begin next year. Apply with a CV and expression of interest to hello@akindaco.com.
- **Guest lectures** are offered into higher education organisations.

## People

- Rana Kökçinar — Senior Psychotherapist, Family Therapist and Education Lead. Leads the education program, author of all research listed above, has taught psychology students at the University of Adelaide since 2023. Master of Clinical Family Therapy; Master of Counselling and Psychotherapy; BMedSci, BSc (Hons); IFS Level 1; Registered Clinical Counsellor PACFA no. 10524; AAFT.
- Paula Gillespie-Fotheringham — Founder and Managing Director, Art Psychotherapist, Specialist Positive Behaviour Support Practitioner, Adjunct Lecturer at the University of Adelaide.
- Kate Maitland — Psychotherapist, Preschool Boost Lead. Master of Counselling and Psychotherapy, University of Adelaide.
- Shane Fotheringham — Co-Director, Clinical Family & Systemic Psychotherapist, Registered Social Worker, former university lecturer. Clinical Member AAFT; Registered Social Worker AASW.
- Also teaching and co-facilitating: Alisha Banks (Principal PBS Consultant), Jade Forgan (Psychotherapist, DBT Lead), Makaela Nolan (Art Therapist), Ann Ibrahim (Psychotherapist), Sophie Johnson (Counsellor), Amy Heffernan (Psychotherapist and Counsellor).
